title: Instagram Reels Social Listening: What 10 Tools Index (2026)
summary: Instagram Reels social listening runs through Meta's narrow API. We read 10 tools' docs: 5 name Reels, none document public Reel comments or video analysis.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Instagram Reels social listening is narrower than most feature lists suggest: in the vendors' own documentation, five of ten popular tools (Brandwatch, Talkwalker/Lumen, Sprinklr, Emplifi, Brand24) say they collect Reels, mostly through hashtags or accounts you connect, while the other five (Meltwater, Sprout Social, Awario, Mentionlytics, Determ) say only "Instagram" or "hashtags". None of the pages we reviewed documents comment text on public Reels or transcription of Instagram Reels. That fits Meta's API limits of 30 hashtags per account per week and a 24-hour window.


You ask a vendor about Instagram. The answer is yes. You assume that means Reels, and everything people say inside them.


It does not. Meta decides what outside tools can see, and its API is far narrower than a feature list implies.


A Reel that never carried your tracked hashtag can stay invisible, even when the creator says your brand out loud. The gap is easy to miss until something goes wrong. It is the blind spot behind[untagged video mentions](https://syncly.app/blog/how-to-measure-untagged-video-mentions) .


So we read the documentation instead of the feature pages: Meta's developer docs plus 10 listening tools' own documentation. Below, we cover what Meta allows, which tools name Reels, what the pages say about analyzing the Reel itself, and a test you can run in any trial.


## Why "Instagram" on a feature list says little about Instagram Reels social listening


A feature list says little because Meta gives third-party tools only two doors to public Instagram content: hashtag search and Business Discovery. Everything else comes from accounts you connect or from an undisclosed arrangement.


**Door 1, hashtag search:** a tool can query up to **30 unique hashtags** per Instagram Business or Creator account in a rolling 7-day period (Source:[Meta Hashtag Search guide, 2026](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-api-with-facebook-login/hashtag-search) ). The` recent_media` edge returns only media published in the **last 24 hours** , up to **50 results per page** , public posts only, with no promoted media (Source:[Meta recent_media reference, 2026](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-api/reference/ig-hashtag/recent-media) ).


Each result carries a caption, a like count and a comment *count* , not comment text. The tool also needs Meta's Instagram Public Content Access feature, which requires app review.


Meta's hashtag docs describe photos and videos (media types IMAGE, VIDEO and CAROUSEL_ALBUM) and never use the word Reels. Five vendors say Reels arrive through hashtags, among other routes, which is plausible. But that proof sits on the vendor side, not in Meta's docs.


**Door 2, Business Discovery:** a tool can pull basic metadata and metrics for other professional accounts, but only accounts you name one by one. It returns comment, like and view counts, never comment content (Source:[Meta Business Discovery guide, 2026](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-api-with-facebook-login/business-discovery) ).


**Your own account** is a separate path: apps can read the comments, posts, reels and stories your own professional account created (Source:[Meta Instagram Platform overview, 2026](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/overview) ). That covers owned analytics, not market listening.


Our reading of Meta's docs, not a Meta quote: public content you do not own offers no caption keyword search, no transcript, no comment text and no firehose. A vendor that reaches further would be using its own crawler, partner data or scraping, and none of the pages we reviewed describes one. For platform differences, see[TikTok, Reels and Shorts compared](https://syncly.app/blog/tiktok-vs-reels-vs-shorts) .


> **Indexing a Reel** : a social listening tool indexes a Reel when the Reel itself (caption, metadata and, where permitted, its comments) becomes a searchable record that matches your query. Naming Instagram on a feature list does not count, and neither do the analytics of an account you own. Indexing what a Reel *says or shows* is a separate capability: video analysis.


We sort every vendor claim onto a five-level ladder:


1.


**Owned data** : Reels and comments from accounts you connect.


2.


**Public discovery** : hashtags or named accounts.


3.


**Reels named** : the vendor's own docs use the word.


4.


**Comments on Reels** : comment text, not counts.


5.


**Video analysis** : transcripts, on-screen text or visual detection on the Reel.


Five of ten tools reach level 3. No page we reviewed documents levels 4 or 5 for public Reels.


## Which social listening tools name Instagram Reels, and which only say Instagram?


Five of ten name Reels in their own Instagram documentation: Brandwatch, Talkwalker/Lumen, Sprinklr, Emplifi and Brand24. The other five say only "Instagram" or "hashtags". Hootsuite, which announced its acquisition of Talkwalker in April 2024 (Source:[Social Media Today, 2024](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/hootsuite-acquisition-social-listening-provider-talkwalker/712613/) ), documents its listening product as Lumen, so we list them together.

**5 of 10** name Reels, and even those lean on hashtags or accounts you name. Sprinklr says earned collection is restricted to hashtags, calls it a channel limitation imposed by Meta, and keeps comments to owned accounts (Source:[Sprinklr help, 2026](https://www.sprinklr.com/help/articles/instagram/instagram-as-a-listening-source/63e38da1a9d5117903016666) ). Emplifi collects Reels through all five of its methods (Source:[Emplifi Reels FAQ, 2026](https://docs.emplifi.io/platform/latest/home/reels-faq) ), across a database of 9,000,000+ Instagram Business and Creator accounts, yet its docs say Reel comments are not included (Source:[Emplifi docs, 2026](https://docs.emplifi.io/platform/latest/home/listening-data-sources-available-coverage) ). Brandwatch announced Reels coverage for owned accounts, non-owned Business accounts and hashtags in a product update dated Aug 1, 2022 (Source:[Brandwatch product update, 2022](https://www.brandwatch.com/blog/brandwatch-product-update-summer-2022/) ).


**0 of 10** document comment text on public Reels, and **0 of 10** document video analysis that runs on Instagram Reels. Where the pages document comments at all, they point to owned accounts (Brandwatch's Consumer Research wording is the one ambiguous case), and Brand24 and Determ keep counts only. Lumen's catalog of 150,000 indexed public Business and Creator accounts collects no comments or replies (Source:[Hootsuite help, 2026](https://help.hootsuite.com/hc/en-us/articles/26832372094619-Data-sources-and-social-media-coverage) ).


The five "Instagram-only" vendors are not necessarily weaker. Their pages are silent, and that is the finding.


**How we verified:** each row traces to the vendor's own documentation, meaning help centers, product pages and release notes. The Meltwater and Sprout Social rows rest on fewer pages because their help centers block automated access.


## Which tools analyze the Reel itself? Three gaps the feature pages hide


None of the pages we reviewed documents transcription, on-screen text reading or visual detection that runs on Instagram Reels. Three gaps stand out.


**Gap 1, the hashtag gate:** in the pages we reviewed, most "Reels covered" claims mean Reels carrying a tracked hashtag, from the last 24 hours. Lumen says a new hashtag channel backfills only the previous 24 hours (Source:[Hootsuite help, 2026](https://help.hootsuite.com/hc/en-us/articles/26832372094619-Data-sources-and-social-media-coverage) ). Determ says it cannot gather posts older than 24 hours (Source:[Determ, 2026](https://determ.com/blog/track-instagram-with-determ/) ). A Reel that never used your hashtag stays invisible on this route.


**Gap 2, no documented Instagram video analysis:** Sprinklr's support table, as we read it, lists Instagram Visual Insights on Videos as enrichments only (object, scene and activity detection), with logo and text data fetching marked unsupported. That would mean logo and text detection cannot find new mentions there.


Brand24 documents spoken-word transcription for TikTok only (Source:[Brand24 changelog, 2026](https://updates.brand24.com/discover-more-tiktok-mentions-with-video-transcriptions-345893) ). Talkwalker and Meltwater advertise video or visual detection without naming Instagram. The Brandwatch and Meltwater pages we reviewed do not document transcription. For what that costs you, see[audio and visual listening](https://syncly.app/blog/audio-vs-visual-social-listening) .


**Gap 3, marketing says more than the help center:** Sprinklr's blog says its Instagram listening captures posts, comments, hashtags, Stories, Reels and visual content. Its help center says earned collection is hashtag-only, comments are owned-only and earned Stories cannot be fetched.


Brandwatch splits the same way. Its Consumer Research page lists comments and Reels for public Business accounts, while Listen's help page says public accounts return posts but not comments and never mentions Reels. The likeliest reading is that "comments" there means counts. When two pages disagree, trust the help center, because it is the page tied to Meta's limits.


## How to test a vendor's Instagram Reels social listening coverage before you sign


Run a three-case trial test, then get written answers.


1.


**Post test Reels** from an Instagram Business account covering three cases: a tracked hashtag, the brand name only in spoken audio, and the brand name only as on-screen text. One Reel per case keeps the results clean.


2.


**Wait 24 hours** , then check which of the three cases each vendor surfaces.


3.


**Ask in writing:** does your Instagram collection use hashtag search, Business Discovery, partner data or your own crawler?


4.


**Ask in writing:** is Reel comment text captured for non-owned accounts?


5.


**Ask in writing:** do transcription, OCR and logo detection run on Instagram Reels, and on which plan?


6.


**Ask in writing:** what is the backfill for a brand-new hashtag?


7.


**Ask which answers go in the contract.**


## What to look for next in Instagram Reels coverage


The real question is whether a tool builds its Reels coverage around the hashtag gate or around the video itself. Hashtag-gated coverage tells you what people tagged. Video-level coverage has to tell you what people said and showed.


[Syncly Social](https://syncly.app/social) covers a video platform set of TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts as part of its[social listening platform](https://syncly.app/social/solution/social-listening) . We left it out of the table on purpose: this is an audit of other vendors' documentation. Run the same three-case test on any vendor, Syncly included.


## Key Takeaways


-


Meta gives outside tools two doors to public Instagram content, so, as we read the docs, "Reels covered" usually means Reels with a tracked hashtag from the last 24 hours.


-


**5 of 10** tools name Reels in their own docs. The other 5 say only "Instagram" or "hashtags". "Unspecified" is an answer, not a no.


-


**0 of 10** document public Reel comment text or Reels video analysis on the pages we reviewed.


-


When a vendor's blog and help center disagree, believe the help center.


-


Run the three-case test and get answers in writing before you sign.


Instagram Reels social listening runs through a narrow gate, and vendors say little about it. The documentation we reviewed shows Reels collection by hashtag and named account, and it does not cover comment text or video analysis on public Reels. The question to ask is not whether a tool covers Instagram. It is whether the tool reads the Reel or only the tag.
